profiles.what: Runs premium flexible and managed workspace centres across India. It had 58 operating centres at the end of FY26 and 72 by July 2026.
how: Rent from customers who use its centres: Rs 173.6 Cr of Rs 201.3 Cr operating revenue in FY26, about 86%.
Other operational income (ancillary services): Rs 27.6 Cr, up from Rs 5.4 Cr.
Food and beverage sales are negligible: Rs 15.5 lakh.
Asset-light model: landlords pay for the fit-outs, Innov8 supplies the brand, demand generation, design and operations. That is how it opened a new centre roughly every three weeks.
numbers: Operating revenue FY26: Rs 201.3 Cr, up 76% from Rs 114.5 Cr
EBITDA net of lease: Rs 49.4 Cr, up from Rs 30 Cr
Net profit: Rs 13.8 Cr vs Rs 1.2 Cr (the headline says Rs 13.7 Cr, the article body says Rs 13.8 Cr)
profiles.watch: Profit quality: other income was Rs 38.9 Cr, including a Rs 36.7 Cr gain on terminating lease contracts. Without that gain the profit jump would look much smaller. The article gives growth drivers as more centres, higher occupancy and better pricing.
profiles.lesson: Landlord-funded capex lets a service business scale fast, but revenue is really rent-spread income, so occupancy and lease terms decide the margin.

profiles.what: Lending-tech platform founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan. Offers digital personal and business loans up to Rs 5 lakh, health-related insurance products and secured loans against property. Got regulatory approval in July 2026 to distribute mutual funds through subsidiary Invincible Minds.
how: The article does not give a revenue split.
Inferred, not from the article: as an NBFC, its core income is interest and fees on the loans it makes; insurance and mutual fund distribution would add commissions.
numbers: Board approved Rs 832.19 Cr preferential issue: 2,64,93,882 shares at Rs 314.11 to 34 investors and entities (subject to regulatory and shareholder approval)
Listed about four months ago at a 11.7% premium to the Rs 171 IPO price; the IPO was Rs 850 Cr fresh issue plus Rs 76 Cr OFS
Computed: Rs 314.11 is about 84% above the Rs 171 IPO price

Named investors: Axis funds (about Rs 200 Cr), MIT via two entities (Rs 85 Cr), Ashoka WhiteOak-linked entities (about Rs 75 Cr), Envision Capital (about Rs 40 Cr), First Bridge (Rs 20 Cr), plus 360 One, Alchemy, Groww, Bandhan Small Cap, Unity Small Finance Bank
profiles.watch: The company did not say how it will use the money. Fresh capital for a lender usually funds loan growth, but that is inference.
profiles.lesson: A quick follow-on raise four months after listing at a much higher price shows institutional demand; the missing use-of-proceeds disclosure is the open question.

profiles.tagline: Audio and microdrama OTT, IPO cleared by SEBI
profiles.what: Founded in 2018 by Lal Chand Bisu, Vikas Goyal and Vinod Meena. Offers audiobooks, podcasts and original audio shows under Kuku FM, plus microdrama platform Kuku TV and microlearning platform Guru. Content library of 20,000+ titles in seven languages; it claims 1 Cr+ listeners and creators and 400 Mn app downloads across its portfolio.
how: The article does not explain the revenue model.
Not stated: whether income comes from subscriptions, pay-per-content or ads. Check the DRHP when it becomes public.
numbers: SEBI issued its observation letter on Friday 11 September 2026 (go-ahead to proceed with the public issue)
IPO size per sources: Rs 2,500-3,500 Cr ($261-366 Mn); possible valuation Rs 15,000 Cr (about $1.8 Bn)
Confidential DRHP filed in June; issue = fresh shares plus offer for sale

Raised over $156 Mn so far; last round $85 Mn Series C in October 2025 led by Granite Asia; investors include Fundamentum, Krafton, Vertex Ventures, IFC, 3one4; MS Dhoni is an investor and Kuku TV brand ambassador
Microdrama market forecast: $1.5 Bn today to $6.5 Bn by 2033 (article's figure)
profiles.watch: Fresh-issue money is planned for tech, AI infrastructure, content production and geographic expansion. Competitors named: Pocket FM, Flick TV, ReelSaga, Miniplix and OTT majors (Amazon, JioHotstar, Zee5).
profiles.lesson: Read the DRHP for revenue split, content cost and cash burn before forming a view; that is where the business model is actually disclosed.

profiles.what: Founded in 2018 by aerospace engineers Gurushankara KC, Abhinav Alva and Chetan Kumar. Develops small gas turbine engines (20 kgf to 400 kgf thrust) for aerial platforms and energy systems, with the design, assembly and testing pipeline and its engine control unit built in-house. Expanding into hydrogen-based technology and distributed power generation, including a 60 kW turbogenerator with a hydrogen flexi-fuel combustor developed with IISc.
how: Sells engines to OEMs: the company says it already has orders from Indian and global OEMs but did not disclose names or values.
Inferred: revenue is hardware sales; the article gives no pricing or revenue figures.
numbers: Raised Rs 43 Cr (about $5.1 Mn), led by Avaana Capital with Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing
Flight trials targeted for Q4 2026
Says it is the first Indian private company pursuing independent airworthiness certification for gas turbine engines under CEMILAC (a DRDO lab)
profiles.watch: Pre-revenue-scale hardware: certification timelines and first commercial deliveries are the milestones to track. Article also notes rising investor interest in aerospace and spacetech (D-Propulse Rs 25 Cr in January; InspeCity Rs 100 Cr in August).
profiles.lesson: Deeptech hardware raises small rounds against long certification cycles; orders without disclosed values are a claim, not yet revenue.

profiles.tagline: Test-prep coaching chain owned by BYJU'S parent
profiles.what: Gurugram-based test-prep brand for engineering and medical entrance exams, owned by BYJU'S parent Think & Learn since its 2021 acquisition.
how: Coaching fees: Rs 1,956.2 Cr of Rs 2,040.5 Cr operating revenue in FY26 (about 96%, computed).
Franchisee revenue: Rs 84.4 Cr, up 4% (about 4%, computed).
numbers: Operating revenue FY26: Rs 2,040.5 Cr vs Rs 2,032.1 Cr (+0.4%)
Net loss: Rs 186.5 Cr vs Rs 220.8 Cr

Loss before exceptional items and tax: Rs 243.5 Cr vs Rs 292.9 Cr; after a Rs 23.3 Cr exceptional charge, pre-tax loss Rs 266.8 Cr; a Rs 80.3 Cr deferred tax credit brought the final loss to Rs 186.5 Cr
Other income more than doubled to Rs 113.7 Cr, driven by a Rs 76.1 Cr write-back of provisions or liabilities and a Rs 19.7 Cr lease remeasurement gain
Total expenses: Rs 2,397.8 Cr, up about 1%
profiles.watch: The smaller loss came from one-off accounting gains, not from the business growing: revenue is flat. Ownership is entangled in the BYJU'S group's disputes: Byju Raveendran proposed relinquishing his claimed interest in 17.89 Mn Aakash shares to settle Qatar Holding's arbitration claim of over $235 Mn; lenders (Global TLB lenders via GLAS Trust) are reportedly in advanced talks for a 30% stake valuing Aakash at about $2 Bn.
profiles.lesson: Separate operating performance from other income and write-backs before believing a loss 'narrowed'. Also: a healthy subsidiary can be dragged into a parent's creditor fight.

profiles.what: Curefoods runs brands such as EatFit, Nomad Pizza, Sharief Bhai Biryani, CakeZone, Frozen Bottle and Krispy Kreme (India rights acquired last year), with 500+ kitchens in 70 cities. Rebel Foods runs Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, Oven Story, Sweet Truth and 20+ other brands across 10 countries.
how: Both report 'operating revenue' from operating cloud kitchens and restaurant chains, i.e. selling food under their own brands.
The article gives no split between delivery, dine-in or other channels.
Costs named as main drivers: material costs, employee benefits, depreciation and amortisation.
numbers: Curefoods FY26: operating revenue Rs 916 Cr (+23% from Rs 746 Cr); net loss Rs 192 Cr (up from Rs 170 Cr); expenses Rs 1,127 Cr
Rebel Foods FY26: operating revenue Rs 1,952 Cr (+20.7% from Rs 1,617 Cr); net loss Rs 282 Cr (down from Rs 337 Cr); expenses Rs 2,266 Cr
Computed loss as share of revenue: Curefoods 21.0% (22.8% a year earlier); Rebel 14.4% (20.8% a year earlier)
Curefoods paused its Rs 800 Cr IPO plans (ET report, 8 June) months after Sebi approval
profiles.watch: Growth is above 20% but both still lose money. Rebel is narrowing losses; Curefoods' loss grew in absolute terms.
profiles.lesson: Food brands scale by adding kitchens, but the test is loss as a percentage of revenue trending toward zero, not revenue growth alone.

profiles.tagline: US health-insurance startup for small businesses (YC winter 2020)
profiles.what: AI-powered platform that helps small businesses choose and manage 'level-funded' health plans, integrating with payroll and HR systems. Level-funded sits between fully insured (carrier bears all risk, higher and predictable cost) and self-funded (employer bears cost, unpredictable): the business makes predictable payments, is insured against unusually high costs, and may get a share of the surplus back if claims stay low.
how: The article does not say how Angle itself earns its revenue.
It says the startup serves 5,000+ businesses and is profitable.
numbers: $200 Mn Series C plus a $400 Mn tender offer (employees can sell some shares) at a $2.7 Bn valuation
Led by Vitruvian Partners; also Town Hall Ventures, Blumberg Capital, Portage Ventures, PruVen Capital and Y Combinator
Round expected to close later in September 2026
profiles.watch: A profitable, non-'AI agent' company raising a large Series C is unusual per TechCrunch. The tender offer is liquidity for staff, not money into the company.
profiles.lesson: Profitability plus a clear, regulated-market wedge (small-business health plans) can still command a large valuation.
